verdict.rationale: Statsig ships Dynamic Configs as a first-class object alongside boolean Feature Gates. Their values can be retrieved through the HTTP API and the SDKs, and experiments serve one or more test variants (A/B/n), so non-boolean, multivariate serving is clearly part of the product. Missing for 10: any documentation of the supported value types (strings, numbers, JSON objects) in a Dynamic Config, a documented multivariate flag construct outside experiments, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve multivariate flags and dynamic configuration values (strings, numbers, JSON), not just booleans

citations.quote: Overview of the Statsig HTTP API for retrieving feature gate, experiment, and dynamic config values and logging events directly without an SDK.
Use target apps in Statsig SDKs to scope feature gates, experiments, and dynamic configs to specific applications inside a single project.
